high.title: Dollar Rises to R$5.11 on Global Risk-Off in Markets
high.summary: The USD/BRL exchange rate closed Friday's session at R$5.1112, marking a 0.24% appreciation of the dollar against the Real. The move was driven by a broad global risk-off environment, with the greenback strengthening across major currency pairs despite some easing in U.S. Treasury yields. The DXY index — which measures the dollar against a basket of six major currencies including the euro and sterling — was trading with gains around 5:00 PM Brasília time, pulling BRL and other EM currencies weaker.

medium.title: Doubts Over AI Boom and War Weigh on Markets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Retreats Today (July 17)
medium.summary: Global markets are trading in the red, driven by a fresh round of selling in semiconductor stocks amid growing concerns over the return on AI investments. Risk appetite is further dampened by escalating geopolitical tensions, with the United States conducting its sixth consecutive day of strikes in the Middle East. The article specifically notes the Ibovespa retreating in USD-denominated terms, which is relevant for international investors assessing combined equity and FX exposure to Brazil. The risk-off environment globally could pressure the BRL and weigh on the Ibovespa, as foreign investors reduce exposure to emerging market assets. Fund managers should monitor whether global risk aversion translates into capital outflows from Brazil, which would add depreciation pressure on BRL/USD and potentially widen Brazilian sovereign spreads.

medium.title: Eurozone Inflation: Annual CPI Slows to 2.8% in June, Confirming Preliminary Reading
medium.summary: Eurozone annual CPI decelerated to 2.8% in June from 3.2% in May, confirming the flash estimate and in line with analyst expectations, though still well above the ECB's 2% target. While this is a developed-market data point, it carries indirect relevance for Brazilian markets: slower Eurozone inflation supports the case for ECB rate cuts, which could influence global liquidity conditions and risk appetite for emerging market assets including BRL-denominated instruments. A more accommodative ECB stance may modestly improve the external environment for Brazil, supporting capital flows into EM fixed income. However, the persistence of inflation above target suggests the ECB will remain cautious, limiting the near-term boost to global EM risk sentiment.

medium.title: Wall Street Pressures Ibovespa, Which 'Holds Firm' With Petrobras (PETR4) Support and Closes Slightly Lower; Dollar Rises to R$5.11
medium.summary: The Ibovespa closed Friday's session down a marginal 0.06% at 173,714.08 points, with losses contained primarily by Petrobras (PETR4), which acted as a defensive buffer amid a risk-off global backdrop and options expiration pressure on blue-chip names. On a weekly basis, however, the index retreated 2.33%, reflecting a more challenging environment for Brazilian equities. The concurrent rise of the dollar to R$5.1112 underscores the external pressure weighing on the market. For equity investors, Petrobras' stabilizing role is notable — any shift in oil prices or domestic fuel pricing policy could remove this support. The weekly loss of 2.33% warrants attention as a potential trend signal if external risk aversion persists into next week.

medium.title: Safra Cuts Price Targets for CSN (CSNA3) and CSN Mineração (CMIN3): What to Do With the Shares?
medium.summary: Banco Safra significantly cut its year-end 2026 price target for CSN (CSNA3) from R$11.30 to R$6.10, while maintaining a neutral recommendation — the new target still implies ~19.6% upside from the prior close. For CSN Mineração (CMIN3), the target was trimmed from R$5.80 to R$5.40, implying approximately 1% downside, also with a neutral stance maintained. The cuts reflect a reassessment of sector outlook, likely tied to softer iron ore prices and deteriorating margins. While CSN and CMIN3 are not major Ibovespa index movers, the downgrades are relevant for mining/steel sector positioning and reflect broader commodity headwinds that could also pressure Vale-related sentiment in the near term.
